messages.subject: sflist2stanfit() and other functions
parts:
A few days ago I submitted a changed get_sampler_params() function and a new plot_sampler_params() function. Of course I'm rewriting them because of the release of Stan 2.0 (furthermore, "my" get_sampler_params() was ugly, because I wrote it in a great hurry...)

But I'd like to understand a preliminary issue.
I always use mclapply() and sflist2stanfit(): four chains are created and then merged.  The sflist2stanfit() help page says that "The ‘stanfit’ objects to be merged need to have the same configuration of iteration, warmup, and thin, besides being from the same model."

Of course, one could say, but it's not really so because the code checks for different n_save and warmup2, not for different iter, warmup, thin. Two chains, the one with iter = 100, warmup = 50, thin = 1 and the other with iter = 1000, warmup = 500, thin = 10 "have equal length of iterations [n_save] and warmup [warmup2]": this is what the code actually checks for.
But it's just a minor issue, I suppose.

I'm wondering if I could set different sampler parameters (now named "controls": adapt_*, metric, stepsize, etc.) for different chains. Could it make sense?
BTW, setting different algorithms would be somewhat sinful, but could happen...

If the answer is "no", then sflist2stanfit() should check for such differences. And I could get (algorithm and) controls from the first chain, as traceplot() and other functions do.
It the answer is "yes", then... I should report (algorithm and) controls for each chain in my functions ;-)

Thanks
Sergio

> A few days ago I submitted a changed get_sampler_params() function and a new plot_sampler_params() function. Of course

> I always use mclapply() and sflist2stanfit(): four chains are created and then merged. The sflist2stanfit() help page
> says that "The ï¿½stanfitï¿½ objects to be merged need to have the same configuration of iteration, warmup, and thin,

> besides being from the same model."
>
> Of course, one could say, but it's not really so because the code checks for different n_save and warmup2, not for
> different iter, warmup, thin.

The code's doing the right thing.

We (or at least I) hadn't anticipated this use case.

But it does bring up an issue of how to report what goes into
the fit object in the print().

> Two chains, the one with iter = 100, warmup = 50, thin = 1 and the other with iter = 1000,
> warmup = 500, thin = 10 "have equal length of iterations [n_save] and warmup [warmup2]": this is what the code actually
> checks for.
> But it's just a minor issue, I suppose.

It's important for two reasons. First, we want our doc to match
what the code does. Second, we want to make sure we preserve
the property of sampling from the posterior.

> I'm wondering if I could set different sampler parameters (now named "controls": adapt_*, metric, stepsize, etc.) for
> different chains. Could it make sense?
> BTW, setting different algorithms would be somewhat sinful, but could happen...

Should be totally OK. As long as each one's a proper set
of draws from an MCMC chain.

> If the answer is "no", then sflist2stanfit() should check for such differences. And I could get (algorithm and) controls
> from the first chain, as traceplot() and other functions do.
> It the answer is "yes", then... I should report (algorithm and) controls for each chain in my functions ;-)

Right --- that's what I meant by reporting what goes into the fit()
object.

- Bob
